status: Scope transcription and dependency map only; universal mathematics pending independent analytic/adversarial gates.

main_claim.source: Published PDF Theorem 1, p.2, equation (3); full abstract p.1.
process: Two independent centered continuous Gaussian standard fractional Brownian motions
main_claim.observations: G_(T,n)=σ(Bⁱ_(jT/n): i=1,2; j=1,…,n). Both complete uniform grids include T. There are n observations per component, or 2n random scalar observations total.
main_claim.target: X_T=∫₀ᵀ B¹_s dB²_s, canonical iterated integral defined by L² limit of piecewise-linear lifts.
main_claim.functions: φ(x)=x⁴(1−x)⁴ on [0,1], zero elsewhere; f=φ′ and g=φ. The zero extensions belong to W^(3,1), with L_r=‖r‖₁ and N_r=‖r‴‖₁. The body specifies this finite regularity; the abstract adjective smooth should not be interpreted as C∞.
main_claim.optimal_estimator: Taking F=E[X_T|G_(T,n)] gives the minimum conditional root mean-square residual bound.

interfaces.mechanism: Established area existence, Chen relation, and polygonal identification
interfaces.source: Paper §2, pp.2–3; NTU journal Proposition 6, printed p.229; Remark 10, p.230; Theorem 2, p.226, with proof pp.237–240; underlying Unterberger Theorem 4.10.
interfaces.input: Independent equal-H standard fBm, H>1/4; analytic approximations converge in Lp and preserve Chen relation.
interfaces.output: Square-integrable area with joint scaling and stationarity; identification with the canonical polygonal lift.
interfaces.remaining_math_gate: Check exact integral orientation, normalization, and law. No exact Euler coefficient is required.

interfaces.mechanism: Sufficient L² convergence of left sums
interfaces.input: I1; finite c₀; |c₁|≤c₀ by Cauchy–Schwarz; differentiated covariance only between separated cells r≥2.
interfaces.output: L_m→X_T in L² in three regimes split at H=3/4. Brownian H=1/2 is handled separately. P_m=L_m+Q_m with Q_m→0.
interfaces.remaining_math_gate: Check the finite lag identity, separated-cell limit, and rate bounds, including empty sums, critical H, and Brownian H.

interfaces.mechanism: Normalized Gaussian representation and dual covariance paths
interfaces.input: 0<D_H<∞ for 0<H<1; conjugate-symmetric real Hilbert space; negative-sign Fourier transform; zero-extended polynomials in W^(3,1).
interfaces.output: Standard fBm law and E[B_t W(u_h)]=h(t)−h(0), using conjugation in u_h.
interfaces.remaining_math_gate: Check normalization, conjugation, Fourier inversion, and weak endpoint derivatives.

interfaces.mechanism: Simultaneous upper Gram bound by periodization
interfaces.input: Integer translations of f and g, scaled by Δ^H; Fourier decay bounded by min(L_r,N_r|η|^(−3)); α∈(3/2,3).
interfaces.output: Gram matrix ≤M_r I uniformly in cell size and count, where M_r=D_H P̄_r/(2π).
interfaces.remaining_math_gate: Check Tonelli, finite trigonometric Parseval, the alias-series bound, and scale powers. This is an upper bound, not rough-increment lower coercivity.

interfaces.mechanism: Quadratic Gaussian witness independent of the complete grid
interfaces.input: All cell paths vanish at every observation time; joint Gaussianity and independence of the two components.
interfaces.output: Y=Σ U_j V_j is independent of G_(T,n), has mean zero, and satisfies E[Y²]=tr(AC)≤nM_fM_g.
interfaces.remaining_math_gate: Check independence from the entire observation vector and the PSD trace bound with signed off-diagonal entries. Cell independence is not assumed.

interfaces.input: I2 with fixed T,n,j; U_j V_j∈L²; deterministic Riemann–Stieltjes convergence.
interfaces.output: E[X_TY]=na(T/n)^(2H) and E[FY]=0 for every L² grid estimator; the stated lower bound follows with the displayed c_H.
interfaces.remaining_math_gate: Check the fixed-mesh limit, positive exact pairing a, and transfer from the enlarged Gaussian realization to the original joint law. No simultaneous m,n limit or stochastic Fubini step is asserted.

boundaries.scope: Excluded. The paper notes a diagonal contribution T/4 to the polygonal-correction second moment. No endpoint canonical construction or lower bound is asserted.
Excluded. Harmonic normalization diverges, and degenerate fBm paths are linear, so the endpoint product recovers the iterated integral.
Included. Independent-component Itô and Stratonovich iterated integrals agree. The prior exact optimum T/(2√n) is stronger than the displayed witness constant.
Included. The sufficient convergence bridge has a logarithmic factor; the stated lower bound does not acquire a logarithmic factor.
Included directly. Each component supplies only the observation at T.
Every positive real T is covered. RMS scales as T^(2H). No T=0 conclusion is needed.
The halved antisymmetric area X_T−B¹_TB²_T/2 has the same optimal conditional residual. The unhalved difference has twice that residual. Factors must be retained when changing the target.
No theorem for nonuniform or adaptive grids, unequal H, correlated components, missing components, additional observations, or arbitrary Gaussian linear information is asserted.
No sharp constant, exact normalized limit, limiting law, uniform positivity in H, or uniform endpoint control is asserted.
